implemented_requirements.evidence: ReversiGame.__init__ creates a SIZE×SIZE board (SIZE = 8) and sets board[3][3]=WHITE, board[3][4]=BLACK, board[4][3]=BLACK, board[4][4]=WHITE.
self.current = BLACK in ReversiGame.__init__; switch_player() toggles via opponent(); main loop calls game.switch_player() after each move.
ReversiGame._flips computes flips for a candidate square; valid_moves() builds a dict of all empty squares with non‑empty flip lists; is_valid_move() uses _flips.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flipping opponent discs when a move is applied
implemented_requirements.evidence: apply_move() calls _flips, places the player's disc, then iterates over the returned coordinates setting them to the player.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when board is full or no valid moves remain
implemented_requirements.evidence: board_full() checks every cell; game_over() returns True if board_full() or neither player has a valid move (has_valid_move).
score() counts BLACK and WHITE pieces; ui.render() appends a line with the scores; ui.announce_result() prints final scores.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Console UI for move entry and board rendering
implemented_requirements.evidence: ui.render() builds a textual board with '*' for valid moves; ui.parse_move() converts user input to coordinates; main.py drives the loop and prints prompts.
computer_move(game) selects the move with the most flips; main.py uses it when mode 2 is chosen and current player is WHITE.

judge.summary: The submitted files contain a complete, runnable Reversi implementation. Core game mechanics—board setup, turn alternation, move validation, disc flipping, end‑game detection, and scoring—are all present and exercised by the console driver. A simple greedy AI is also provided. No show‑stopper bugs are evident, so the solution meets the benchmark requirements.
